nodes.label: release workflow (v* tags and dry runs)
nodes.rationale: workflow_dispatch is a dry run: it builds and smokes everything but publishes nothing, so the whole release path can be exercised without cutting a tag.

nodes.label: build-binaries job (linux x64/arm64, darwin arm64)
nodes.rationale: fail-fast is off so one arch failing does not cancel the other's evidence. Intel macOS is omitted on purpose (scarce free Intel runners would stall releases; Intel Macs use --docker/--source). A compiled asset probe proves the binary can materialize embedded runtime assets out of $bunfs for spawned children — the env.md ENAMETOOLONG landmine class — and is deleted before checksum/upload so it never ships.

nodes.label: update-flow job (update -> swap -> rollback e2e)
nodes.rationale: Hermetic e2e on REAL compiled binaries: builds two versions, serves a local versions.json over HTTP, then asserts the on-disk version transition and its reversibility. Deliberately has no `needs` so it runs in parallel as validation; x64 only because one arch is enough to exercise the real cycle.

nodes.label: docker job (multi-arch GHCR image)
nodes.rationale: Builds linux/amd64 + linux/arm64 via QEMU/buildx and pushes only on a tag; `latest` is only tagged for tags.

nodes.label: build-android job (signed release APK)
nodes.rationale: Versioning is automated on CI with no manual versionCode bump: versionName = the v* tag, versionCode = ANDROID_VERSION_CODE_FLOOR (1000) + GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER so it strictly increases and stays above any historical local default. Missing signing/Firebase secrets degrade gracefully to the debug key and placeholder google-services.json so the build still assembles (push breaks, upgrades break). Values are written to dist/android-client.env so versions.json matches the APK actually built.

nodes.label: build-desktop-linux job (jpackage .deb)
nodes.rationale: The Compose Desktop app carries its own packageVersion independent of the v* tag, so the asset name stays stable. KCEF (~100-150MB embedded Chromium) is downloaded on first editor use rather than bundled in the .deb.

nodes.label: build-desktop-windows job (WiX .msi + native host)
nodes.rationale: jpackage cannot cross-build MSI, so windows-latest (with WiX preinstalled) is the only place it can be produced. Bun is pinned to 1.3.14 because ConPTY/EOF behavior is a native-Windows release gate. The broker typecheck is continue-on-error against a documented TS 5.9/@types-bun baseline so an otherwise-valid MSI lane is not permanently red; focused tests and the packaged-helper assertions gate instead.

nodes.label: build-desktop-macos job (native SwiftUI Supermux.app DMG)
nodes.rationale: Signed inside-out (helpers, Shared.framework, appex, main binary, then the bundle) with a throwaway keychain deleted in an always() step. Tag builds hard-fail without Developer ID + notary secrets; workflow_dispatch without them still uploads an explicitly *unsigned* DMG so the lane is useful before secrets exist.

nodes.label: build-compose-desktop-macos job (Compose Multiplatform DMG)
nodes.rationale: Distinct bundle id (dev.supermux.desktop) and asset name so it installs side-by-side with the native SwiftUI app on a case-insensitive volume. Compose's signing preflight resolves the identity by common name (label), not SHA-1 — the opposite of raw codesign against a non-default keychain. Compose signs the .app but not the outer DMG, which Gatekeeper still needs signed.

nodes.label: build-ios-testflight job (archive, export .ipa, upload)
nodes.rationale: The iOS app bundles no broker/tmux/frpc (sources exclude Host/** and HostResources/**), so there is no staging step. TestFlight requires CFBundleVersion to strictly increase, so CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION is overridden with TESTFLIGHT_BUILD_OFFSET (1000) + GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER to land above the old headless-Mac flow. Uses a dedicated App Manager ASC key rather than the mac job's notary key, which may be notarization-scoped and would 403 on upload. Absent secrets on a tag only WARN so binary/docker releases keep shipping.

nodes.label: assign-testflight job (attach build to beta group)
nodes.rationale: altool --upload-app only hands the .ipa to App Store Connect; a build belonging to no beta group is NOT installable however VALID it looks — that gap silently stranded every CI build between 1040 and 1061. Runs on Linux via plain ASC REST so the multi-minute PROCESSING wait costs 1x runner minutes instead of macOS's 10x.

nodes.label: publish-website job (versions.json + pinned compose)
nodes.rationale: Pushes versions.json and a tag-substituted docker-compose.yml to the supermux-website repo; skipped with a warning when WEBSITE_PUSH_TOKEN is absent so a missing secret never fails the release. Android version is read from dist/android-client.env (the value CI actually baked in) rather than re-derived from gradle defaults.

hyperedges.label: supermux release pipeline (build, sign, publish across every platform)
